export const meta = {
  name: 'codex-chatgpt-signin-feasibility',
  description: 'Web research: can Codex CLI use ChatGPT-subscription sign-in for headless/agent use instead of a pay-as-you-go API key',
  phases: [
    { title: 'Investigate', detail: 'web research on Codex CLI sign-in model, limits, community recipes' },
    { title: 'Synthesize', detail: 'feasibility verdict + how-to + limitations' },
  ],
}

const LENSES = [
  {
    key: 'official-signin',
    prompt: `Research the OFFICIAL OpenAI Codex CLI sign-in model (2025-2026). Use web tools (ToolSearch to load WebSearch, WebFetch, and/or perplexity / search-hub web_search_exa). Answer precisely with source URLs:
1. Codex CLI supports two sign-in paths: signing in with a ChatGPT account (Plus/Pro/Team/Enterprise) vs. providing a pay-as-you-go API key. How does the ChatGPT sign-in flow work ('codex login'), and where does it store the resulting session on disk (the config directory under the user's home)?
2. Can NON-INTERACTIVE / headless invocation ('codex exec', and Codex running as an MCP server / app-server) use the ChatGPT-account session, or does programmatic use REQUIRE an API key? Is there a config setting (config.toml 'preferred_auth_method' with values like 'chatgpt' vs 'apikey') that forces the ChatGPT session?
3. Session lifetime: how long does the ChatGPT sign-in session stay valid, how is it refreshed, and does refresh work without a browser (for headless machines)?
Return markdown 'CODEX SIGN-IN — OFFICIAL' with a clear yes/no on ChatGPT-session use for programmatic/agent contexts, exact commands/config keys, and cited URLs. Grade confidence per claim; mark anything you cannot confirm as UNVERIFIED.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'limits-tos',
    prompt: `Research LIMITATIONS, quotas, and Terms-of-Service for using a ChatGPT-subscription sign-in (rather than a pay-as-you-go API key) with the OpenAI Codex CLI in AUTOMATED / agent / headless contexts (2025-2026). Use web tools (ToolSearch -> WebSearch/WebFetch/perplexity). Answer with sources:
1. Usage limits when Codex runs under a ChatGPT Plus / Pro / Team subscription vs. under API billing: are there 5-hour and weekly windows? What are the rough message/task caps per tier? Which models are available under the subscription vs. only via the API?
2. Does OpenAI's usage policy permit driving the ChatGPT-subscription session from automation / multi-agent orchestration / CI, or is subscription access intended for interactive use? Any documented risk of throttling or account action for automated subscription use?
3. Reliability in headless: session-expiry mid-run, refresh failures, 401/403 problems.
Return markdown 'LIMITS & TOS' with concrete numbers/quotes where available, cited URLs, confidence grades, and UNVERIFIED flags.`,
  },
  {
    key: 'community-headless',
    prompt: `Find recent (2025-2026) COMMUNITY reports (GitHub issues/discussions, forum threads, blog posts) about running the OpenAI Codex CLI HEADLESS / in CI / inside an agent orchestrator using the ChatGPT-account sign-in rather than a pay-as-you-go API key. Use web tools (ToolSearch -> WebSearch/WebFetch, firecrawl_research_search_github, or search-hub web_search_exa).
Answer:
1. Concrete working setups people use to run 'codex exec' non-interactively under a ChatGPT sign-in (moving the session/config between machines, config.toml preferred_auth_method, environment). Are there proven recipes?
2. Reported gotchas: session refresh in headless, portability of the sign-in session across machines, 'codex login' needing a browser, exec sandbox/approval flags.
3. Any tooling that bridges Codex's ChatGPT-session auth into agent frameworks.
Return markdown 'COMMUNITY HEADLESS RECIPES' with concrete steps, source URLs, and how battle-tested each recipe is.`,
  },
]

phase('Investigate')
const findings = await parallel(
  LENSES.map((l) => () => agent(l.prompt, { label: l.key, phase: 'Investigate' })),
)
const good = findings.filter(Boolean)

phase('Synthesize')
const report = await agent(
  `Write the FINAL feasibility report answering: "Can Codex agents/sessions authenticate via the ChatGPT-subscription sign-in instead of a pay-as-you-go API key, for headless/agent use, and should they?"

Synthesize STRICTLY from these investigator findings (do not invent). Where findings conflict or a claim is single-sourced, say so.

FINDINGS:
${good.map((f, i) => `### Investigator ${i + 1}\n${f}`).join('\n\n')}

Produce markdown:
# Codex ChatGPT sign-in vs API key (headless/agent) — Feasibility
## Verdict
YES (fully supported) / PARTIAL (works with caveats) / NO — one line + 2-3 sentence justification.
## How the sign-in works (official)
ChatGPT sign-in vs API key; where the session lives; config.toml preferred_auth_method; whether codex exec / app-server honor the ChatGPT session; session refresh.
## Steps to switch to the ChatGPT sign-in
Concrete ordered commands + config edits (Windows), including anything an agent-orchestration wrapper would need so it does not force an API key.
## Limitations & risks
Rate limits (subscription vs API), model access, ToS on automated subscription use, headless refresh reliability. Flag UNVERIFIED items.
## Recommendation
For a user who runs Codex as a parallel agent alongside Claude (quality>cost, budget-paced across weekly windows): switch, hybrid (ChatGPT-session primary + API-key fallback), or keep API key — and why.
## Sources
Numbered URLs with confidence tiers.

Keep it tight and decision-useful.`,
  { label: 'synthesize', phase: 'Synthesize' },
)
return report
result:
# Codex ChatGPT sign-in vs API key (headless/agent) — Feasibility

## Verdict

**PARTIAL (works with caveats) — technically fully supported, operationally brittle, contractually grey.** All three investigators agree the mechanism works: every Codex entry point (`codex`, `codex exec`, `codex mcp-server`/app-server) shares one cached login at `~/.codex/auth.json`, and if that holds a ChatGPT sign-in, an API key is not required (Inv. 1, HIGH). The caveats are real and independent: headless *initial* login needs a workaround, subscription usage is capped by 5-hour + weekly windows, the backend is undocumented and can change without notice, and OpenAI's own guidance steers automation to API keys.

## How the sign-in works (official)

- **Two auth paths.** `codex login` offers "Sign in with ChatGPT" (subscription: Plus/Pro/Team/Business/Enterprise, routes through `chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses`) vs "Provide your own API key" (usage-based, `api.openai.com/v1/`). ChatGPT sign-in is a standard OAuth loopback — browser redirects to a local callback (port **1455**), which is why it fails on browserless boxes (Inv. 1 HIGH; Inv. 2/3 HIGH).
- **Where the session lives.** `~/.codex/auth.json` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json`), a plaintext OAuth bundle (access + refresh + id token) by default, or the OS keychain. Directory is `$CODEX_HOME` (default `~/.codex`). Backend is configurable: `cli_auth_credentials_store = "file" | "keyring" | "auto"`. The **CLI, IDE extension, and MCP/app-server all share this one file** (Inv. 1, HIGH).
- **`codex exec` and app-server honor the ChatGPT session.** Docs state `codex exec` "reuses saved CLI authentication by default" (Inv. 1, HIGH). `codex mcp-server` shares the same `Config`/`$CODEX_HOME`, so it also runs on the cached ChatGPT session — confirmed by shared-auth architecture, though **no single doc sentence states this as bluntly for mcp-server as for exec (doc-phrasing UNVERIFIED)** (Inv. 1).
- **Config key to force the ChatGPT session — CONFLICT between investigators, flagged:**
  - **Inv. 1 (HIGH, issue #3286):** the task's named key `preferred_auth_method = "chatgpt"` was **removed in Codex CLI 0.35.0** and is now **ignored**; the replacement is **`forced_login_method = "chatgpt"`** (note the API value is `api`, not `apikey`). Post-0.35, "the last login method is always assumed to be your preferred method."
  - **Inv. 3** still lists `preferred_auth_method = "apikey"|"chatgpt"` (added 2025-08-18) as a live key "picks which to use when both exist," without noting its removal.
  - **Reconciliation:** Inv. 1 explicitly traces the timeline (added Aug 2025 → removed 0.35.0) and is the more specific source; Inv. 3's mention appears to draw from the older issue (#2760). **Treat `forced_login_method` as current; assume `preferred_auth_method` is legacy/inert on any recent Codex.** Verify against your installed version.
- **Session refresh.** Proactive: Codex refreshes the token bundle if `last_refresh` is older than **~8 days**, using the stored refresh token — **no browser needed** — and rewrites `auth.json` in place, plus a 401 refresh-and-retry fallback (Inv. 1 HIGH; Inv. 3 corroborates ~8–10 day access-token staleness, refresh token lasting weeks-to-months). **Refresh-token hard maximum lifetime is UNVERIFIED** (not published; ~8 days is the refresh *trigger*, not a proven expiry ceiling).

## Steps to switch to the ChatGPT sign-in (Windows)

1. **Interactive first login (box with a browser):**
   ```
   codex login          # choose "Sign in with ChatGPT"
   ```
   Writes `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json`.
2. **Headless/no-browser first login — pick one:**
   - `codex login --device-auth` (beta; prints URL + code to authorize from any device). **Prerequisite:** a workspace owner must enable "Device Code Authorization" in ChatGPT security settings, or it fails (Inv. 3 HIGH; Inv. 2 flags admin-disable as a hard blocker, issue #9253).
   - **Seed the file:** run `codex login` on a machine with a browser, copy `auth.json` to `%USERPROFILE%\.codex\auth.json` on the target, restrict perms. Works and is the de-facto CI method (Inv. 3 HIGH).
   - SSH-forward port 1455 (`ssh -L 1455:localhost:1455 …`) for a one-time remote login (Inv. 3, community, HIGH).
3. **Force file-backed, portable storage** in `~/.codex/config.toml`:
   ```toml
   cli_auth_credentials_store = "file"
   forced_login_method = "chatgpt"   # current key; blocks silent API-key fallback
   ```
   (Do **not** rely on `preferred_auth_method` — see conflict above.)
4. **Run non-interactively:** `codex exec --full-auto "…"` (or `--json` / `-o file` for machine-readable output). It reuses `auth.json` automatically.
5. **What an agent-orchestration wrapper must do so it does *not* force an API key:**
   - **Do not set `OPENAI_API_KEY` or `CODEX_API_KEY`** in the job/process env — `CODEX_API_KEY` is read by `codex exec` and overrides the cached session; a stray key also causes mixed-auth contamination with proxies (Inv. 1, Inv. 3).
   - **Persist the *refreshed* `auth.json`, never re-seed from the stale secret each run** — overwriting throws away the rolled-forward tokens Codex just wrote and breaks auth (Inv. 1, Inv. 3, both HIGH).
   - **One `auth.json` per runner / serialized stream** — two machines sharing one copy rotate each other's refresh token and break auth (Inv. 3 HIGH).
   - **Don't hardcode a `-codex` model default:** under ChatGPT auth, `gpt-5-codex`/`gpt-5.1-codex`/`gpt-5.3-codex` can return HTTP 400 "not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account"; use the account-allowed model (e.g. `gpt-5.5`) (Inv. 3, MED).
   - macOS-only trap (not Windows): a detached child Codex can't reach the Keychain → "Authentication required"; forces file-store or a key (Inv. 3).

## Limitations & risks

- **Rate limits (subscription vs API).** Subscription is capped by a **5-hour rolling window (primary) + a stacked weekly cap**, and **CLI/web/IDE share the same window** — a heavy agent run competes with your interactive usage (Inv. 2, HIGH). Post-April-2026 repricing moved to token/credits; per-tier message counts are **dynamic ranges, and exact weekly numbers are UNVERIFIED** (not published). API-key mode has **no windows** — pure per-token billing — which is OpenAI's recommended automation path (Inv. 2, HIGH).
- **Model access.** Newest models land on the **subscription route first** (GPT-5.5 was subscription-only at launch — "the semi-official Codex backdoor API"); API mode gets new models on a **delay and strips cloud features** (GitHub/Slack/Codex cloud). Conversely, **models can be pulled from the subscription route without notice** mid-workflow (Inv. 2, MED–HIGH; issue #25839).
- **ToS on automated subscription use — genuinely ambiguous, no clean written permission for unattended CI (Inv. 2).** *For:* Codex CLI is Apache-2.0 (fork/modify fine), and OpenAI DevEx lead Romain Huet publicly endorsed using "Codex, and their ChatGPT subscription, wherever they like" (HIGH) — **but that endorsement is scoped to interactive third-party *clients*, not unattended CI or multi-account pooling.** *Against:* the Terms forbid "automatically or programmatically extract … Output" and "circumvent any rate limits," which an aggressive reading covers (whether it's *intended* to cover official-CLI automation is **UNVERIFIED** — OpenAI hasn't drawn the line). **Multi-account pooling / credential sharing to dodge windows is the clear red line.** A May–July 2026 wave of Codex/Pro account bans is documented, but **causation is UNVERIFIED** (several look like quota-bug false positives).
- **Headless refresh reliability.** Usable but brittle: **getting logged in is the hard part** (localhost-callback failure → device-auth, which an admin can disable workspace-wide = hard blocker; issue #9253 HIGH). Mid-run refresh is claimed robust but is **single-sourced (danielvaughan) and UNVERIFIED against an OpenAI primary source** (Inv. 2/3). The backend endpoint is **undocumented with no SLA** and unstable behind SOCKS5 proxies. No confirmed recurring mid-run 401/403 failure mode was found (**UNVERIFIED**).
- **Enterprise escape hatch.** ChatGPT **Business/Enterprise** can mint `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (shipped May 2026) — truly browserless, RBAC-governed, the *sanctioned* headless answer — but requires an Enterprise workspace and admin enablement (Inv. 1/3). Not available to individual Plus/Pro.

## Recommendation

**Hybrid — ChatGPT-session primary, API-key fallback — for this user's profile.** The user's use case (Codex as a parallel agent alongside Claude, quality > cost, **budget-paced across weekly windows**) maps directly onto the subscription model: the 5-hour + weekly caps *are* the exact pacing cadence, and subscription buys newest-model-first access plus "free" windowed usage that the per-token API doesn't. Single-user, single-account, interactive-style automation of *your own* subscription via the official CLI is tolerated in practice (Huet + Apache license), and this profile is far closer to that than to unattended multi-account CI.

Keep an **API key wired as fallback** (via `CODEX_API_KEY` on the specific `codex exec` invocation, exec-only) for the failure modes the findings make concrete: window exhaustion, a model getting pulled from the subscription route, or refresh breaking on a headless runner. This preserves budget-pacing benefits while covering the brittleness.

**Hard constraints:** (1) run **one account per session** — do **not** pool multiple ChatGPT accounts through a proxy (the clear ToS red line + the plausible ban vector); (2) **persist the refreshed `auth.json`, never re-seed from the stale secret**; (3) migrate any config off `preferred_auth_method` to `forced_login_method` after verifying your installed version. *Do not switch fully off the API key* — the undocumented backend, model-pull risk, and unverified refresh robustness make subscription-only automation too fragile for a load-bearing parallel agent.

## Sources

**Official / primary (HIGH):**
1. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth — auth model, ChatGPT vs API, `auth.json`, refresh
2. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth/ci-cd-auth — run `codex exec` as Codex account in CI; seed-and-persist; ~8-day refresh trigger
3. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/non-interactive-mode — `codex exec` reuses saved auth; `CODEX_API_KEY` (exec-only)
4. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/config-file/config-reference — `forced_login_method`, `cli_auth_credentials_store`, `chatgpt_base_url`
5. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens — `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (Business/Enterprise, browserless)
6. https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540 — Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan
7. https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001106 — Codex rate card (Apr-2026 token/credit repricing)
8. https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing — plan tiers
9. https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ — "What you cannot do" (verbatim ToS clauses)
10. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3286 — `preferred_auth_method` removed in 0.35.0 → `forced_login_method`
11. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/9253 — device-auth admin-disable = hard headless blocker
12. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/3820 (+ #2798) — headless-auth CI friction ("pushing you to OPENAI_API_KEY")
13. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25839 — GPT-5.3-Codex pulled from subscription accounts
14. https://x.com/romainhuet/status/2038699202834841962 — "wherever they like" endorsement (scope: interactive clients)
15. https://github.com/openai/codex/discussions/8338 — Apache-2.0; fork/modify OK (not a ToS ruling)
16. https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/2760 — config-key origin (`preferred_auth_method` added 2025-08-18; exec flags)

**Secondary (MED — corroborating, blogs/community):**
17. https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/04/24/... — endpoint routing, refresh, pooling grey area, undocumented backend
18. https://simonwillison.net/2026/Apr/23/gpt-5-5/ — GPT-5.5 "semi-official Codex backdoor API"
19. https://www.developersdigest.tech/blog/codex-exec-ci-headless-guide — headless CI guide, ~8-day staleness
20. https://blog.codekunda.com/posts/codex-cli-headless-vps/ · https://github.com/codertesla/codex-remote-login — port-1455 SSH-tunnel recipes

**LOW / UNVERIFIED (flagged inline):**
21. https://community.openai.com/t/codex-chatgpt-pro-account-banned-... (+ related threads) — 2026 ban wave, **causation unverified**
22. https://github.com/tuannvm/codex-mcp-server/issues/192 · https://github.com/dicklesworthstone/ntm/issues/154 — HTTP 400 model-refusal under ChatGPT auth
